notes.note: An empty list cannot be written: by rule B.1.5.1-020a "[]" is not an empty list, and invalid metacharacter combinations keep their literal value (no format error). A reject test is therefore impossible; the test shows that "[]a]" is the list {']','a'} instead of an empty list.
Same as 019a for the negated list: positive test that "[^]a]" is not an empty negated list. Uses the batch reading of 020b (both '^' and ']' literal).
Chosen reading: in "[^]...]" both '^' and ']' are literal members (consistent with list item B.1.5.1-024a). The last sentence of NOTE 2 (B.1.5.1-034a) could suggest the caret still negates.
\b inside a set expression is not tested because its meaning there (word boundary vs. a single character) is undefined; all other listed metacharacters are tested.
Only the quadruple form \q{group,plane,row,cell} is tested, as listed in the standard.
